Full read of all 11 files in /home/user/ringweave/lib/src/core (index, graph, budgets, constraints, greedy, constrainedGreedy, metrics, polish, bounds, rng, swap) plus lib/test and lib/CLAUDE.md, then built the lib into .review-scratch and ran hostile inputs against the compiled output.

Attacks that FAILED to break it (all verified by running, not by reading):
- Pre-gate work on the polish paths: `polishConstrained(ring(1e6), cons, {iters:0})` returns in 176 ms and `polish(ring(1e6), {maxIters:0})` in 53 ms — `checkPolishSize` + `boundedPolishIterations` genuinely bound the fixed sweeps. `polishConstrained` does build `input.edgeList()` before the size gate (unlike `polish`, which deliberately uses `degrees().reduce`), but the edge list is emitted already sorted so the sort is linear and the residual is ~120 ms at MAX_ROSTER — not a hang.
- `polish`/`polishConstrained` iteration knobs: `maxIters` = Infinity / 1e9 / NaN / -1 / non-integer are all reduced to <= MAX_POLISH_ITERS by `boundedPolishIterations`; the anneal calibration's `trials` is itself capped by `maxIters`, so pre-loop work is at most 2x the loop budget. `polishIters` cannot be used to ask for MORE work than the default.
- `checkPolishSize` cannot be made to throw out of either public builder: at every (n,k) their own gates admit, the fixed sweeps are <= 2.25e8 against a 8.65e8 budget.
- Worst auto-polish configurations (those exactly at MAX_POLISH_WORK): buildBuddyGraph(60,22) 10.7 s, (120,4) 26.6 s, (111,5) 23.4 s — the k-aware gate holds, no repeat of the old 33 s (120,12) case.
- Constrained work budget: measured (5000,4) 21.7 s, (464,463) 78.3 s, (1000,100) 37.6 s, (2000,25) 30.5 s. All four sit at ~1.7x the figures documented on MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK, i.e. a uniform machine factor across a 5x spread of shapes — `constrainedWork` is shape-correct and I could not find an accepted (n,k) that beats the documented corner.
- `validate` ordering: `structuralReasons` -> MAX_ROSTER -> MAX_CONSTRAINED_N -> k -> MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK -> O(n^2) connectivity walk. The walk is genuinely last; n=5000 with one prohibited pair is 115 ms, with 2M prohibited pairs 1.2 s. `Constraints(1e6)` is refused before any O(n^2) work. No pair array is materialized more than a constant number of times.
- `constrainedGreedy`'s `completionCap = n*k*6` cannot be turned into a spin: every iteration either adds an edge or breaks, and k = 2**53 / -0 / 0 all terminate immediately. `forceConnect` is genuinely inert (completion exits legal-edge-maximal).
- Numeric edges: `-0` for n and k (behaves as 0 throughout, no asymmetric branch), non-integer/Infinity/NaN n, k, `mind`, `seed`; `greedyWork`/`constrainedWork` never overflow to Infinity inside the admitted range; the `Int32Array(n*n)` in ringGreedy is unreachable above ~18 MB because MAX_GREEDY_WORK refuses first; `mooreLowerBounds` terminates for k=1,2 and non-integer input.
- Determinism: `choosePartner`, `deficientVertices`, `edgeList`, `proposeSwap` all use total orders; the only Set-iteration-order dependence is inside `forceConnect`/`joinAnyComponents`, which is proven and asserted inert.
- Untrusted text: lib has no string sink at all. The only user-supplied strings are `Tag` values in `fromTags`, which are compared with `===` and never emitted; `formatReason` interpolates numbers only. Nothing in lib/src can reach CSV, a clipboard, a filename or the DOM.

Read every file under lib/src/core (graph.ts, budgets.ts, constraints.ts, greedy.ts, constrainedGreedy.ts, polish.ts, swap.ts, rng.ts, metrics.ts, bounds.ts, index.ts) plus lib/CLAUDE.md, docs/PROJECT_PLAN.md, docs/findings/churn-priors-weight.md, and app/CLAUDE.md's "Known follow-ons" (to see what the sibling component has already discovered about this exact boundary, so as not to re-file it).

Concretely attempted two extensions against the real tree, not just read the code:
1. The declared OCP seam (`constraints.ts`'s `TagPolicy` switch in `Constraints.fromTags`): patched in a second variant (`require_same`, mirroring `prohibit_same`'s loop but calling `c.require` instead of `c.prohibit`), added the case to the `TagPolicy` union, ran `npm run typecheck` (clean, no other file touched) and the full `npm test` suite (243/243 passed unmodified — greedy/polish/graph/index files untouched), then built `dist` and exercised it live: `Constraints.fromTags(6, ["A","A","A","B","B","B"], "require_same")` produced the two required triangles, `validate` returned no errors, and `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph` returned `report.satisfied: true` with all 6 required edges present. Reverted the patch afterward (scratch script + backup left under `.review-scratch/`, working tree clean per `git status`). This is a genuine positive result: the seam pays exactly as `lib/CLAUDE.md` claims — a new tag policy costs one `case`, zero changes to `legalEdge`, `constrainedMeasure`, `greedy.ts`, `polish.ts`, or `index.ts`.
2. Traced the next real committed feature that touches the core specifically: F9 "recalculate with minimal disruption" (PROJECT_PLAN.md M4, flagship). Confirmed via `docs/findings/churn-priors-weight.md` that the entire prior-preservation mechanism the F9 default is benchmarked and tuned against (`DEFAULT_PRIOR_WEIGHT`, `Constraints.addPrior`/`priorHard`, `polishConstrained`'s `priorWeight` term) lives exclusively on the constrained tier (`buildConstrainedBuddyGraph`/`constrainedGreedy`/`polishConstrained`). Grepped `polish.ts` and `index.ts`'s `BuddyOptions`/`PolishOptions` for any prior/history concept — none exists; `polish()` (the unconstrained, ring-greedy-seeded, Moore-optimal fast path) has no way to bias toward a previous edge set, hard or soft. Confirmed via grep that `app/src` has zero live references to `priorWeight`/`addPrior`/`priorHard` — the app's own CLAUDE.md already names this exact gap under "Known follow-ons" as deliberately deferred, with real unresolved design questions (name-resolution across a changed roster, promote-before-validate hazard), so I did not re-file that app-side deferral. What app/CLAUDE.md does not record is the core-level shape of the gap: the fast/default tier has structurally no prior-preservation channel at all, so *any* future F9 implementation — even for a roster that has never used a single required/prohibited constraint — must permanently switch that roster onto the weaker general-purpose greedy (losing `girth`/`asplGap`/Moore-bound optimality, and changing the result's shape) the first time it is recalculated with "preserve buddies" on.

themes.theme: Work-budget gates that are supposed to stop attacker/caller-controlled (n,k)-style parameters from driving unbounded core computation are inconsistently applied and miscalibrated across generation entry points: one exported generator has no gate at all, the gate's own cost estimator is shaped wrong so it underprices roughly half the inputs it admits, and another entry point pays the O(n^2) cost before its gate can run.
findingSummaries: repairDegrees(g,k,minDist) is exported public API with no validation of k and no MAX_GREEDY_WORK-style check, unlike its sibling ringGreedy which refuses the same (n,k) pair.

greedyWork(n,k) in budgets.ts is not proportional to ringGreedy's real work -- the ratio of actual operations to charged budget rises from ~1.06 at the calibration point to ~2.34 at the worst admitted (n,k), so MAX_GREEDY_WORK lets through inputs costing over 2x what it claims to bound.

Constraints.fromTags materializes an O(n^2) set of prohibited pairs inside the constructor, before validate() (which holds MAX_CONSTRAINED_N/MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK) ever runs, so the gate that exists cannot refuse the cost it's meant to bound; currently unreachable from untrusted input (fromTags has no callers in app/src).
themes.remediation: Move the existing budget check earlier and reuse it everywhere instead of writing new checks: hoist validate()'s MAX_CONSTRAINED_N/MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK check (and an n/pair-count precheck) to the first statement of fromTags before its double loop runs, and make repairDegrees call the same greedyWork/MAX_GREEDY_WORK check ringGreedy already calls, at its top, before doing any BFS-scan -- collapsing three divergent gating paths into the one check-before-work ordering ringGreedy already demonstrates, and fixing greedyWork's formula itself rather than adding a second, more accurate estimator alongside it.

themes.theme: An untrusted, caller-chosen vertex index reaches bfsDistances -- the one vertex-index-taking export that skips the checkVertex guard its siblings shortestPath and eccentricity already call -- turning an out-of-range index into an opaque native TypeError instead of the module's own clear refusal.
findingSummaries: bfsDistances is exported from index.ts and is the only vertex-index-taking export that does not call checkVertex; an out-of-range source index makes dist[s]=0 a no-op and g.adj[u] undefined, throwing an unlabeled TypeError instead of a clear bounds error.
themes.remediation: Add the single call checkVertex(g, s, "source") as the first statement of bfsDistances, matching the call shortestPath and eccentricity already make -- no new check logic, just extending the existing guard to the one call site missing it.

themes.theme: The committed minimal-disruption-recalc feature (F9) has no path on the default/fast unconstrained tier because the only prior-preservation machinery (addPrior/priorHard/priorWeight) was built exclusively into the weaker constrained tier, meaning any future implementation permanently forces a plain roster onto the constrained tier and away from girth/asplGap guarantees the moment 'preserve buddies' is used.
findingSummaries: buildBuddyGraph/polish has no priors/history concept in its option surface or objective; all prior-preservation machinery lives on buildConstrainedBuddyGraph/constrainedGreedy, which the F9-grounding benchmark already depends on, so any roster needing 'preserve buddies' must route through the constrained tier and lose Moore-bound-based metrics from that point on.
themes.remediation: Do not add a second prior-bias mechanism to the unconstrained tier; instead, when F9 lands, delete the implicit assumption that a plain roster can stay on the fast tier once 'preserve buddies' is requested -- document (in lib/CLAUDE.md, not just app/CLAUDE.md) that using F9 always promotes onto the single existing constrained-tier prior mechanism, removing the need for a parallel implementation.

themes.theme: The TagPolicy type advertises a 'require_same' value that Constraints.fromTags' switch statement does not implement, so the compiler accepts values the runtime rejects with 'unknown tag policy'.
findingSummaries: TagPolicy type declares 'require_same' as valid, but Constraints.fromTags() throws 'unknown tag policy' when called with it.
themes.remediation: Remove 'require_same' from the TagPolicy type union so the type stops promising a case the switch statement doesn't have, and note the deferral in lib/CLAUDE.md's known-limitations list -- closing the gap by shrinking the type rather than adding the missing switch case.

gating.theme: every generation entry point is supposed to carry both a size cap and a work cap, but one exported generator validates its degree parameter not at all
gating.summary: `repairDegrees(g, k, minDist)` is exported public API and performs no validation of `k` (not even `Number.isInteger`) and enforces no work budget, so a caller-supplied huge `k` drives it to build a near-complete graph one BFS-scan at a time; `ringGreedy` refuses the identical (n, k) pair via `MAX_GREEDY_WORK`.
gating.failure: Measured in /home/user/ringweave/.review-scratch/p10.mjs: repairDegrees(ring(200), 1e9) = 544 ms, ring(300) = 2085 ms, ring(400) = 5642 ms (~n^3.4), extrapolating to hours at n=5000 which MAX_ROSTER (1e6) admits. greedyWork(400, 1e9) = 1.28e10 already exceeds MAX_GREEDY_WORK = 1e10, i.e. ringGreedy(400, 1e9) throws 'too large to generate in reasonable time' while repairDegrees(ring(400), 1e9) runs to completion. repairDegrees(g, NaN) and repairDegrees(g, Infinity) are likewise accepted silently (NaN makes `degree(v) < k` false everywhere, so the pass is a silent no-op rather than a refusal — the same silent-no-op failure mode already fixed for `mind` in ringGreedy and for `priorWeight` in polishConstrained).
gating.remediation: Give `repairDegrees` the same two guards its sibling generators already carry, at the top of the function: reject a non-integer or negative `k` with the wording `ringGreedy` uses, and throw when `greedyWork(g.n, k) > MAX_GREEDY_WORK`. `budgets.ts` already exports both; this is three lines and no new constant. Closing the theme means checking the sibling: `girth` is documented as deliberately uncapped because its cost is fixed by the caller's own Graph, which is a different (and defensible) case — `repairDegrees` differs precisely because its cost is driven by an unvalidated caller-supplied parameter.
gating.invariant: For every graph `g` and every `k`, `repairDegrees(g, k)` either returns having done work bounded by the same budget its only in-tree caller is held to, or throws — machine-checkable as: `repairDegrees(g, k)` throws whenever `!Number.isInteger(k) || k < 0 || greedyWork(g.n, k) > MAX_GREEDY_WORK`, and otherwise returns; equivalently, no (g, k) accepted by `repairDegrees` is refused by `ringGreedy` for the same (n, k).

gating.theme: the generation work budget is not an upper bound on the work it claims to bound — its cost estimator changes shape with k, so the worst input the budget admits does roughly twice the work the budget prices it at
gating.summary: `greedyWork(n,k) = n²·(n·min(k,n-1)/2)` is calibrated at k=4 and is NOT proportional to the operations ringGreedy actually performs. It charges for every edge in a k-regular graph, but the ring seed already supplies n of them, and it does not model that `findPair`'s per-call scan stays ~2n² for dense k while it collapses as vertices saturate at sparse k. The result is that the ratio (real operations / budget) rises from ~1.06 at the calibration point to ~2.34 at the worst admitted configuration, so MAX_GREEDY_WORK admits inputs costing over twice what the constant's own documentation says it buys. This is the primary DoS gate for attacker-chosen (n,k) on the unconstrained path.
gating.failure:
Measured with an operation counter instrumented into a compiled copy of greedy.ts (distance-cache cell writes in `updateAfterEdge` + candidate scans in `findPair`), so the evidence is machine-independent:
  buildBuddyGraph(1000, 4)  -> budget 2.00e9, ops 2.12e9  (ratio 1.06), 6.9 s
  buildBuddyGraph(1000, 20) -> budget 1.00e10, ops 2.19e10 (ratio 2.19), 136.7 s
  buildBuddyGraph(800, 39)  -> budget 9.98e9, ops 2.34e10 (ratio 2.34), 215.7 s
All three are ACCEPTED (greedyWork <= MAX_GREEDY_WORK = 1e10). buildBuddyGraph(800, 39) with default options runs 220.8 s wall-clock against a constant documented as "1e10 is therefore ~60 s worst case"; correcting for this machine's measured ~1.7x factor (established independently against the constrained-path table, which reproduces uniformly) that is still ~130 s, i.e. ~2.2x the stated ceiling. The app-reachable ceiling (1000, 12) measured 67.1 s against a documented 38.5 s. Note the worst case is NOT at either end of the k range the comment's table samples — (500,160) is 55.3 s and (376,375) is 22.0 s — so the table's sampling is what hid it.
gating.remediation: Make the estimator shape-correct rather than lowering the constant (lowering it alone would refuse (1000,12), which ships). Charge the edges ACTUALLY added and the real per-edge scan: `greedyWork(n,k) = 3·n²·max(0, n·min(k,n-1)/2 − n)`. Against the three measured points that estimator has ratios 0.71 / 0.81 / 0.82 — flat to within 15% instead of varying 2.2x. Then recalibrate MAX_GREEDY_WORK to the tightest value that still admits (1000,12), and restate the wall-clock claim from the recalibrated worst point rather than from k=4. Ratchet with an instrumented-counter property test rather than a timing test.
gating.invariant: For every integer (n,k) that `ringGreedy` admits (i.e. n <= MAX_CACHED_N and greedyWork(n,k) <= MAX_GREEDY_WORK), the number of inner-loop operations the run actually performs — distance-cache cell writes in `updateAfterEdge` plus candidate-scan steps in `findPair` — must be <= MAX_GREEDY_WORK. Equivalently: greedyWork must dominate the operation count it is named for, for all admitted inputs, not only at the calibration point. Today (800,39) violates this at 2.34e10 > 1e10.

gating.theme: an untrusted vertex index reaches an exported metric that has no bounds guard, producing a native TypeError instead of the module's own clear refusal
gating.summary: `metrics.ts` defines `checkVertex` precisely because "the path/eccentricity entry points take indices chosen by a caller (ultimately a user selection), and `bfsDistances` would silently tolerate a bad one" — but `bfsDistances` is itself exported from the package index (index.ts line 16) and is the only vertex-index-taking export that does NOT call it. `shortestPath` and `eccentricity` both do. An out-of-range source makes `dist[s] = 0` a no-op on the Int32Array, then `g.adj[u]` is `undefined` and the for-of throws a TypeError that names neither the bad index nor the valid range.
gating.failure: bfsDistances(ring(10), -1) / (…, 10) / (…, 2.5) / (…, NaN) / (…, 1e9) all throw `TypeError: g.adj[u] is not iterable`, instead of the module's own `source -1 must be an integer in [0, 9]`. Not a hang and not a memory-safety issue — a diagnosis-quality failure on the one exported metric whose sibling exports are guarded. No caller in app/src today (the app uses `shortestPath`/`eccentricity`), so this is forward-looking rather than presently reachable.
gating.remediation: Add `checkVertex(g, s, "source")` as the first statement of `bfsDistances`. It is O(1) and the function already allocates an Int32Array(n), so it cannot be on a hot path where the check matters. `girth`'s internal per-source loop and `allPairsSummary` pass loop indices and are unaffected.
gating.invariant: Every exported function in metrics.ts that accepts a vertex index rejects a non-integer or out-of-range index with the module's `<label> <v> must be an integer in [0, n-1]` Error, for all graphs and all index values — no exported metric may surface a native TypeError or return a distance vector derived from an index it never validated.

confirmed.summary: Re-verifying the limitation already recorded in lib/CLAUDE.md, because it is exactly the shape this lens is asked to hunt and the numbers had not been re-measured. `Constraints.fromTags` takes `n` on faith — `degreeOf` in the same file, the `Graph` constructor and `validate` all guard it — and then runs an unguarded double loop that materializes one Set key per same-tag pair. Every gate that could refuse the input (MAX_CONSTRAINED_N, MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK) lives in `validate`, which by construction runs after the constructor has already paid. Filed as deferral, not blocking: `grep -rn fromTags app/src` is empty, so nothing untrusted reaches it in the current tree.
confirmed.failure: Measured against the compiled lib: `Constraints.fromTags(3000, new Array(3000).fill('A'))` builds 4,498,500 prohibited-pair keys in 4,958 ms before returning — `validate` never gets a turn, and at tens of millions of pairs the Set construction itself is the failure. `Constraints.fromTags(-5, [])` and `Constraints.fromTags(2.5, [])` both return without throwing, where `new Graph(-5)` and `degreeOf(-5, …)` refuse. `Constraints.fromTags(4, [NaN, NaN, NaN, NaN])` yields prohibitedCount 0: NaN !== NaN, so a NaN tag silently inverts the documented `prohibit_same` policy rather than grouping.
confirmed.remediation: When a tag UI (F7) lands: validate `n` against MAX_ROSTER/MAX_CONSTRAINED_N as the first statement, then pre-count group sizes in one O(n) pass and refuse against an explicit pair cap (sum of C(size,2) over groups) BEFORE entering the double loop, and coerce non-finite tag values to null so they take the documented "never grouped" path. Until then, keep it out of any untrusted call path.
confirmed.invariant: `Constraints.fromTags` allocates no more than O(n) before it has validated n and refused against an explicit prohibited-pair cap; and for all tag arrays, a tag value that is not equal to itself (NaN) is treated identically to null (never grouped) rather than never matching.

confirmed.theme: the flagship committed feature (F9, minimal-disruption recalc) has no implementation path on the core's default/fast tier — prior-preservation exists only on the weaker constrained tier
confirmed.summary: buildBuddyGraph/polish (the ring-greedy-seeded, Moore-optimal default tier) has no priors/history concept anywhere in its option surface or objective; the only prior-preservation machinery (Constraints.addPrior/priorHard, polishConstrained's priorWeight term, DEFAULT_PRIOR_WEIGHT) lives on buildConstrainedBuddyGraph/constrainedGreedy, which the churn-priors-weight.md benchmark that grounds the F9 product claim already builds on exclusively. So any future 'recalculate, preserve buddies' implementation must route through the constrained tier even for a roster with zero hard constraints, permanently losing girth/asplGap (documented as omitted from ConstrainedBuddyResult because Moore's bound assumes a k-regular target constrained graphs only approximate) and changing the result shape for that roster from that point on.
confirmed.failure: a roster that has never used F7 constraints gets 'preserve buddies' toggled on for one recalc (F9): the app has no way to ask buildBuddyGraph/polish to weight toward the previous edge set, so it must call buildConstrainedBuddyGraph with an all-priors Constraints object instead — the returned ConstraintReport-shaped result has no girth/asplGap, and the underlying algorithm silently changes from ring-greedy (near-Moore-optimal by construction) to constrainedGreedy (general-purpose, ~28% incidental prior retention before polish per the churn benchmark) for that roster going forward
confirmed.remediation: when F9 implementation actually starts (M4), decide explicitly whether the unconstrained tier gains its own lightweight prior-bias (e.g. a priorWeight/priorPairs option threaded into polish()'s objective, mirroring constrainedMeasure) or whether F9 is documented as always promoting a roster onto the constrained tier the first time 'preserve buddies' is used — and record whichever choice in lib/CLAUDE.md's known-limitations list, since it is not currently written down there (only app/CLAUDE.md notes the app-side wiring is missing, not this core-shape consequence)
